content.intro: This lesson covers Guided Lab: Clustering in the Guided Labs and Capstone Preparation module. It preserves the source syllabus topic and subtopics, then adds an original explanation, a runnable reference example, and a practice task.
content.why_it_matters: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct.

content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: The example groups nearby one-dimensional points into two clusters. Cluster labels are arbitrary identifiers, not ordered classes. For guided lab: clustering, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
X = [[0.0], [0.2], [0.1], [8.0], [8.2], [8.1]]
model = KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10, random_state=4).fit(X)
print(len(model.cluster_centers_))

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Check input shapes, target alignment, data types, missing values, label order, and whether the expected output assumes a fixed random seed. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data, preferably inside a Pipeline. Do not select parameters by repeatedly looking at the final test set.
